 SUBJECT:  DIRECTOR AND RECREATION MANAGER REPORT

BACKGROUND

The Community Services Director and Recreation Manager provide a monthly report to the
Recreation Commission. The report provides relevant administrative, operational, and financial
updates, as well as information on upcoming events, marketing and communication efforts, and
customer feedback.

DISCUSSION

Personnel Updates
No updates at this time.

FY 2022-23 Recreation Division Work Plan
As part of the budget development process, each City department provides goals and objectives
or “work plans.” These work plans are then supported by operating and capital improvement
budget requests and are reported on throughout the year, including year-end. In addition to
managing day-to-day facility operations and core program/service delivery, the Recreation
Division has the work plan initiatives laid out in Attachment 1 for FY 2022-23.

New Lacy Park Gatehouse
If you’ve visited the Park recently, you may have noticed the upgrade to the Gatehouse
(admissions booth) at the main entrance. In partnership with the Parks and Public Works (PPW)
Department, staff recently selected and installed a new Tuff Shed that replaces the old structure.
Interior finishes are still in progress (dry wall, flooring, lighting, electrical, HVAC, etc.). In addition,
Recreation staff will work with the PPW Department on upgrades to public signage.

REMINDER: Tickets Still on Sale for Literary Libations – October 15
Please consider attending the San Marino Public Library Foundation’s fall fundraiser event on
Saturday, October 15 at the Crowell Public Library (CPL) from 6 – 9 PM. This ticketed event

  Page 6 of 20
 features an evening of delectable food and wine tastings, a variety of beers and whiskeys, and
literary activities spaced throughout the book stacks. All net proceeds benefit future capital
improvements, as well as advancing technology infrastructure at CPL. For details, please visit
sanmarinoplf.org.

REMINDER: Trunk or Treat & Movie Night – October 28 | 6 – 10 PM | Lacy Park
Pre-sale: R: $5 / NR: $10; Gate Price: R / NR: $15
Join your friends, neighbors, and family for a Spooktacular time! There will be trunk or treating,
food trucks, music, games, crafts, costume contests, and more! Then when the ghouls go to sleep,
a special screening of Hotel Transylvania will be shown on the lawn. Pre-order your wristbands
now through October 27. Pre-ordered wristbands must be picked up at the Stoneman Building
(1560 Pasqualito Drive) by October 28 at 11 AM. Wristbands will also be sold at Lacy Park on
the day of the event. Wristband sales are non-refundable.

Commissioner Volunteers Needed!
We would like to request the assistance of our new Recreation Commissioners to assist at the
Trunk or Treat & Movie Night event. We would greatly appreciate two Commissioners to serve
as costume contest judges from approximately 6:30 – 8:00 PM and two Commissioners to help
hand out goodies at the decorated Recreation Division trunk from 6 – 8 PM. Please contact
Recreation Manager Covarrubias at (626) 403-2200 by Monday, October 24 to join in on the fun.
Thank you so much for the consideration!

REMINDER: Happy Hour Friendsgiving – November 9 | 12 PM | Lacy Park
Join your friends and neighbors for a Friendsgiving luncheon. Enjoy a traditional Thanksgiving Day
feast with music, drinks, and opportunity drawings. Don’t miss your chance to give thanks for
friendships and community. This event is free and open to San Marino residents ages
55+. Registration is required.

Operational Staff Briefings
  Smarter Living Series: Hearing Loss
  On September 14, the Recreation Division hosted a Smarter Living Series lecture at
  Crowell Public Library on the topic of hearing loss. Dr. Norma Camacho provided a
  lesson on the function of our ears, how hearing loss can affect other organ functions,
  and the importance of preventive care. 23 participants learned more about what health
  risks are associated with hearing loss and received an informational packet with various
  resources. Dr. Camacho held a raffle at the end of the lecture and awarded the winner
  with a free set of hearing protection headphones.

  Senior Trip to Catalina Island
  On September 15, the Recreation Division led a senior excursion to Catalina Island. 50
  seniors boarded the Catalina Express to explore the island’s attractions including the town
  of Avalon, shops, and the popular promenade. All participants pre-selected a meal and ate
  lunch at “The Sand Trap.” The reviews of the trip were fantastic, as detailed below.

  Puppy Love Dog PAW-ty
  On September 17, the Recreation Division hosted its second annual Puppy Love Dog
  PAW-ty at Lacy Park and it was a resounding success. There were approximately 650
  two-legged friends in attendance with 170 four-legged pals accompanying them. The
  PAW-ty included music, free giveaways, doggy obstacle courses, plenty of doggy treats,
  and contests. There was a resounding amount of community support and many positive
  comments including “fun event” and “thank you so much for doing this.”

  Page 8 of 20
   Nature Series: Audubon Society Nature Walk
  On September 25, the Recreation Division in partnership with the Pasadena Audubon
  Society hosted its second annual Nature Walk at Lacy Park. 18 people registered for
  this free, guided tour. The Walk was led by Audubon Board Member Luke Tiller who
  reported identifying 24 different bird species and butterflies in the one-mile walk. The
  Pasadena Audubon Society expressed an interest to lead another walk in Spring 2023.

 SUBJECT:  FY 2022-23 PLANNING TIMELINE

BACKGROUND

Staff utilize an organizational tool called a “Planning Timeline” to assist with keeping track of reoccurring
and new agenda items that need to be brought to the Recreation Commission, and in what month.
Some items need to go to the City Council after discussion by the Commission, so it is critical that
items are not forgotten or delayed. The Timeline serves as a great reminder for staff, but it is also a
valuable orientation tool. Understanding its value, staff are sharing the FY 2022-23 Planning Timeline to
help familiarize and educate the Commission.

DISCUSSION

Attachment I is the FY 2022-23 Planning Timeline. Items in black appear on the agenda year over year.
Items bolded and in blue have been added by staff, and may not appear on the agenda year over year.
At the bottom of the document are standing items, which appear on the agenda of every regular
meeting and future items, which have not been calendared out yet.

In addition to sharing this document as an orientation for the Recreation Commission, staff request
that the Commission share any items that they would like discussed or reviewed in the future.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the FY 2022-23 Planning Timeline and recommend
items for future discussion and review. If the Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
appropriate motion would be:

“I move to receive and file the FY 2022-23 Planning Timeline.”

 SUBJECT:  2018-22 PROGRAMS AND SERVICES PARTICIPATION REPORT

BACKGROUND

On an annual basis, staff will provide to the Recreation Commission a summary-level, three to
five-year programs and services “Participation Report.” Due to the impact of the pandemic on
service delivery, staff prepared a 5-year snapshot. The report compiles and analyzes what
programs and services were offered, in addition to providing an interpretation of trends in
participation. In short, this report quantifies the service-level impact (including variances) of all
Recreation Division offerings, which are organized by the following age-delineated program areas:

  •  Aquatics
  •  Summer Camps
  •  Early Childhood 0 – 4 years
  •  Youth & Teen 5 – 17 years
  •  Adult 18+ years
  •  Active Adult/Senior 55+ years
  •  Family – All Ages
  •  Community Events
  •  Facility Rentals
  •  Services

DISCUSSION

The COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent lock-down has had a profound and historic effect on
services worldwide. As the report (Attachment 1) shows, during the majority of 2020 and 2021,
indoor facilities in San Marino remained closed. Outdoor programs were gradually authorized,
although mandated physical distancing became a driving force behind capacity limits. Therefore,
staff deemed those years incomplete and/or severely disrupted for reporting purposes. 2022 is
then benchmarked against the last complete or normal operational year, or 2019. The 2018
numbers were captured, when possible, to provide a 3-year trend.

  Page 14 of 20
 Aquatics
This program area was a resounding success for the Division in 2022. With an 8% increase in
participation from 2019, 1,546 individuals were served in a 9-week period during the months of
June and July. It should also be noted that during 2019, the program was managed by a third-party
contractor and was plagued with ongoing safety and operational issues. This year, City staff took
back the management of the program with great success under the leadership of Recreation
Manager Covarrubias.

Summer Camps
Summer Day Camps are core programs during the summer months, and the Recreation Division
has a well-earned reputation of being an outstanding service provider. While the numbers indicate
an unfortunate decrease of 28%, it is attributed to the Lunch Ride program (transportation from
summer school to camp) that did not get offered due to low enrollment/lack of demand.

Early Childhood 0 – 4 years
This is an area that includes offerings such as pre-school, toddler classes, and tot sports. The
2018 Re-envisioned Plan called for a significant reduction in this area in order to shift staffing
resources to the newly prioritized areas of community events and adult programming. With that,
this program area realized a 51% decrease from 2019.

Youth & Teen 5 – 17 years
Similar to Early Childhood classes, as per City Council direction in 2018, a reduction in youth
contract classes was implemented. Furthermore, the School District sought to become the
primary service provider in San Marino for before and after school care; the City-operated
program was cancelled, in addition to the supporting transportation program, resulting in a 74%
reduction in participation throughout this program area.

Adult 18+ years
There is a 58% reduction in program participation in this program area. It is attributed to the loss
of a very popular instructor, as well as the loss of program space with the temporary closure of
the San Marino Center for renovation. It should also be noted that like the case of this instructor,
several other instructors have yet to return to teaching post-pandemic.

Active Adult/Seniors 55+ years
This program area represents service to anyone 55 years and older with classes meeting
predominantly at the San Marino Center. Due to the pandemic shut-down and San Marino Center
being renovated now through Fall 2023, program offerings such as Bridge, Gentle Yoga, and
Senior Trips have been drastically affected.

Family – All Ages
This is a new program area that reflects a demand for programming targeted to families. Six
programs were successfully offered this year serving 268 participants and mainly held outdoors
at Lacy Park.

  Page 15 of 20
 Community Events
As mentioned in the 2018 Re-envisioned Plan, City Council directed staff to reduce the number
of contract classes and offer more community-building events. In 2021 and 2022, staff did a
phenomenal job of offering six new events that resulted in a 60% participation increase. The new
events were: Home for the Holidays, Lacy Park After Dark Camp Out, Light Up San Marino,
Puppy Love Dog PAW-ty, Summer Concert Series, and Trunk or Treat & Movie Night.

Facility Rentals
This reporting area captures rental usage at four locations: Lacy Park (LP), Stoneman Building,
San Marino Center (SMC), and Crowell Public Library (CPL). Recreation staff, on behalf of CSD,
manage all facility rentals and supportive resources, such as staffing, A/V support, room set-ups
and take-downs, etc. To no surprise, Lacy Park has been a popular outdoor space for rentals,
especially as pandemic restrictions lifted. This resulted in both rental and participation numbers
doubling from prior year. Stoneman Building rentals were discontinued altogether in early 2020
due to the pandemic. City leadership decided to cease any further rental activity due to the poor
condition of the facility. Similarly, the SMC usage was also phased out due to the pandemic and
pending renovation. Lastly, external rentals of the spaces at CPL also dramatically declined
throughout the pandemic; in addition, this facility serves as auxiliary space to the SMC and
supports the City’s need for internal meeting space.

Services
The core support services provided by the Recreation Division include Senior Wellness Calls and
Dial-a-Ride. Close to 900 individuals will be served in these two programs in 2022.

Conclusion
In conclusion, it is estimated that the overall number of people served in all program and service
areas in 2022 will be slightly over 50,000. The sizeable increase from 2019 is due to new
community event offerings, and the Department taking over the management and tracking of Lacy
Park weekend admission (non-resident fee).

Lastly, the best news is that we are well on our way to full recovery to reach pre-pandemic
participation and service levels. This includes the execution of major programming and service-
level adjustments to successfully align with priorities set forth in the Council approved 2018 3-
Year Recreation Re-envisioned Program Plan.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the Program and Services Participation
Report.

MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO RECREATION COMMISSION
  MONDAY, OCTOBER 10, 2022 AT 6:00 P.M.
  BARTH ROOM, CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Yen called the regular meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. in the Barth
Room, located at 1890 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Yen led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Commissioner Wu, Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Tam,
  Vice Chairperson Solan, and Chairperson Yen

  ABSENT: None

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

1. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

Commissioner Wu, Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Tam, Vice Chairperson Solan, and
Chairperson Yen shared a brief introduction of themselves. Chairperson Yen also shared his
thoughts about how the Commission can get the community engaged and involved.

NEW BUSINESS

2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

Commissioner Tsai moved, seconded by Vice Chairperson Solan, to approve the minutes from
September 12, 2022.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Commissioner Wu, Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Tam, Vice Chairperson
  Solan, and Chairperson Yen
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None
 RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
OCTOBER 10, 2022  PAGE 2 OF 3

3. DIRECTOR AND RECREATION MANAGER REPORT

Director Johnson and Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

There was discussion by the Commission concerning the background of the Recreation Re-
Envisioning Plan, its impact on youth and adult programs, and next steps; contract class revenue
split; a potential community interest survey to help determine demand for programs; the need for
staffing in order to increase program levels; the process of converting the aquatics program from
contracted to in-house; and the frequency and type of reporting that the Commission will receive
regarding updates on the Division’s Work Plan.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

4. FY 2022-23 PLANNING TIMELINE

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

There was discussion by the Commission about what can be done to request an increase in staffing
levels in time to be included in the next budget and to determine what programs are in demand by
the community. Vice Chair Solan requested a facility audit to determine areas that can be utilized
for programming. The Commission agreed to talk to neighbors and fellow residents about their
program ideas and discuss findings at the next few meetings as part of the Commissioner Reports.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

5. 2018-22 PROGRAMS AND SERVICES PARTICIPATION REPORT

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

Commissioner Tsai inquired if the capacity and waitlist for each offering can be added to the Report
to assist with interpreting the data. Chairperson Yen asked that the Commission have the
opportunity to provide input on future reporting and share what data they’re interested in seeing,
such as offerings with an extensive waitlist.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None
